content:
I'm Justin, the maintainer of jdhart81/prooflens, an open-source tool for visual explanations of supported Lean statements, developed with AI assistance. I remain responsible for its released behavior and claims.

I've published a builder guide with a reusable example. If you're explaining a theorem to another reader, try one small public or synthetic statement from your own work:

  • Paste it into the browser app under Explore your own Lean; no account, installation or payment is needed.
  • Inspect the assumptions, change an input, and save a chart and Markdown explanation alongside your documentation. The packet includes an actual exported chart and a plain HTML companion-page recipe; leanblueprint authors can try a manual linked companion, with no plugin or automatic build integration claimed.

Source preview does not run Lean or verify proofs. An input ending in sorry remains unproved; numerical charts illustrate selected values. Custom definitions and unsupported syntax may be rejected.

I'd value one concrete report: what question became clearer, or what was the first blocker? Reply here or in the feedback discussion. Use public or synthetic examples, without private research or contact details. Participation is optional, and I'll ask separately before showcasing anyone's words. The guide has maintainer checks; independent useful use is still unconfirmed.
